//: Dirty, torn and tainted cloth (AIR rule, not CDDA's FILTHY flag). A garment or piece of cloth rolled from a loot table may come dirty, torn or tainted; nothing found in a house, a shop, a clinic or the laboratory does, and the wild tables list ragged clothes that always do. Dirty cloth can be worn at a standing cost to the mood (see worn) but goes into no recipe; torn cloth cannot be worn at all; taking either apart gives dirty cloth. Washing clears dirt, never a tear; tainted cloth cannot be washed and its fabric is lost when taken apart. Tables are matched by exact id first, then by the longest listed prefix ending in '*'; unlisted tables leave things clean.

bedding.//: Found bedding (AIR rule, 26.09.2026 evening): a mattress, sleeping bag, blanket or rollmat found in a house, a shop or a clinic, or taken off a bed there, is rarely perfect. Each rolls dirty (the ordinary laundry flag: washable, a long wash) and damaged (a boolean on the instance: a mattress cannot be mended) on its own; the sleep it gives is multiplied by dirtyQuality and damagedQuality, both when both. A mattress from the village shelf is clean and whole. washLitres: the litres of cloth a wash of this piece counts as, where its own volume would make it absurd.

worn.//: Wearing dirty cloth (AIR rule): a standing mood that settles within minutes and stays while any dirty garment is on the body, floorPerGarment for each dirty garment worn down to floorMax (stored units; shown times practice.json morale.scale). Once the last one is off or washed it fades over fadeHours. Torn or tainted cloth is still never worn.

load.//: A load is measured in litres of cloth (the items' own volume), in half-litre steps, never under the minimum.

wash.//: Cold washing with a board or a kit: water, soap and elbow grease. Water and soap are charges per litre of load; soap flakes are lighter, so twice as many go in.

boil.//: Boiling needs no soap and no board, only a vessel that boils and heat under it, but it eats more water, more time and the fuel that time burns.
